title: Spot BTC/ETH ETF net flow shocks and realized volatility
orthogonality: Treatment is the ETF creation/redemption FLOW itself, not the trading-clock / session-structure effect of ETF-ization.
information_set: Forecast origin = 00:00 UTC ending calendar day t. Farside publishes day-t flows ~21:00 UTC on day t, so flow_t and the completed UTC day-t RV are both known; target RV_{t+1..t+h} lies entirely ahead.

BTC.qlike_noise_note: r^2 is a chi^2(1) variance proxy: its QLIKE level runs ~7x that of hourly RV, so it is reported as robustness only.

ETH.qlike_noise_note: r^2 is a chi^2(1) variance proxy: its QLIKE level runs ~7x that of hourly RV, so it is reported as robustness only.

endogeneity_note: Flow is contemporaneously correlated with same-day return and volatility, which is exactly why a contemporaneous OLS of RV on flow would be uninterpretable. All predictive claims below are strictly out-of-sample and conditional on a HAR-RV baseline.

BTC.description: Friday ETF flow -> mean GK RV over Sat+Sun (weekend gap)

ETH.description: Friday ETF flow -> mean GK RV over Sat+Sun (weekend gap)

multiple_testing.gate_note: All counts are gated on the FLOW-FAVOURING direction (DM t < -3). abs(t) > 3 would also count a flow model that is significantly WORSE.

smearing_robustness.note: The alt model has more parameters -> lower training residual variance -> smaller exp(0.5*s2) multiplier -> lower forecasts. QLIKE is asymmetric, so this could manufacture the null. Re-scored with no smearing and with the baseline's smearing forced on both models: the verdict is unchanged, so the null is not an artifact of this transform.

flow_transform_robustness.note: Warther (1995): only the unexpected component of flow should carry news, and netting can hide offsetting creations/redemptions. We test signed, squared, gross-churn and AR(5)-unexpected flow. None beats HAR.

eth_oos_window_sensitivity.note: Primary spec (INITIAL_TRAIN=250) gives ETH only 233 OOS origins, short of the 252-day preamble bar. With INITIAL_TRAIN=200 the OOS window clears the bar; the verdict is unchanged.

full_family_multiple_testing.interpretation: Any single cell that crosses Harvey must be judged against every shot taken in this study, not against its own robustness family.

BTC.interpretation: The DM/Harvey |t|>3 gate turns out to be near-powerless on this target: QLIKE loss differentials are dominated by the huge idiosyncratic noise of daily RV, so even a large injected effect barely moves DM t. Clark-West -- which explicitly corrects the parameter-noise penalty that biases DM toward the smaller model -- DOES have power. The honest power statement for this study therefore rests on the CW gate, and the null means 'no effect as large as the CW MDE', not 'no effect'.

ETH.interpretation: The DM/Harvey |t|>3 gate turns out to be near-powerless on this target: QLIKE loss differentials are dominated by the huge idiosyncratic noise of daily RV, so even a large injected effect barely moves DM t. Clark-West -- which explicitly corrects the parameter-noise penalty that biases DM toward the smaller model -- DOES have power. The honest power statement for this study therefore rests on the CW gate, and the null means 'no effect as large as the CW MDE', not 'no effect'.

power_caveat: The DM/Harvey |t|>3 gate is close to useless on this target. QLIKE loss differentials are swamped by the idiosyncratic noise of daily RV, so the smallest injected effect DM can see is enormous: BTC: +122.55%, ETH: not reached even at +122.55% (RV uplift per 1-sd flow shock). A null resting on DM alone would therefore be nearly vacuous -- it could not have detected even a doubling of RV after a one-sd flow shock in ETH. Clark-West, which corrects the parameter-noise penalty that biases DM toward the smaller model, DOES have power: it clears its gate at BTC: +16.18%, ETH: +16.18%. On the real data CW never exceeds 1.091 (gate 1.645). The null therefore rests on CW, and its honest scope is 'no incremental content as large as the CW minimum detectable effect'.
verdict_basis: 0/10 primary DM tests pass Harvey t<-3 in the flow-favouring direction (0 significantly WORSE than baseline). Clark-West -- the properly-sized test for these NESTED models, and the only gate with usable power here -- supports flow in 0/10 (max CW t on real data = 1.091, gate = 1.645). 0/10 survive one-sided Holm at 5%; 0 of all 46 DM tests cross Harvey favouring flow, 0 survive full-family Holm. POWER: DM/Harvey MDE = BTC: +122.55%, ETH: not reached even at +122.55% (effectively unusable); Clark-West MDE = BTC: +16.18%, ETH: +16.18% RV uplift per 1-sd flow shock. Claim scope: 'no incremental content as large as ~+16% RV per 1-sd flow shock', NOT 'no content whatsoever'.
